## Why visit

A purposeful detour for lovers of local cask, especially mild. The pub showcases Bank Top in the setting of an ordinary two-room community local, with conversation and the beer doing most of the work. That makes it a useful contrast to industrial taprooms and spectacular city-centre interiors. It is outside Bolton’s central station quarter, so go because the brewery and traditional styles interest you, not merely because Bolton is on a map. Pair it with the Olde Man & Scythe if you want a small Bolton route with both beer and historic character.

## Beer

CAMRA documents nine handpumps, mostly Bank Top, with Dark Mild, Flat Cap and Pavilion Pale normally represented plus a guest.

## Cider and perry

**Cider reported; qualification needs checking.** CAMRA explicitly says only some of the boxed/bottled ciders may qualify as real. Do not assume all still cider does.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Not established; do not plan a meal here without checking.

## Plan the visit

Separate from the brewery itself; a pub visit does not imply a brewery tour. Factor in local transport from central Bolton.

**Getting there:** Astley Bridge, reached by local bus from Bolton Interchange rather than a brief station walk.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
